svg.title: From $790,000 Gross Billings to $150,100 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-billings-to-owner-profit; chart type: waterfall; title: From $790,000 Gross Billings to $150,100 Owner Profit; subtitle: Six bars reconcile the 45% retained spread and 19.0% gross-basis margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Formula v2.0 canonical Base totals: $790,000 gross billings, $355,500 retained revenue, and $150,100 annual owner profit. The three operating-expense categories are illustrative allocations totaling $205,400, not supplied line-item forecasts. First and last bars are totals; intervening negative values are deductions. The 45% retained presentation follows the supplied ASC 606 scorecard convention; actual reporting requires the contract-specific principal-versus-agent assessment.; caption: $790,000 − $434,500 − $96,000 − $72,000 − $37,400 = $150,100. Owner profit is 19.0% of gross billings and 42.22% of retained revenue.; stages: label: Gross housing billings; value: $790,000 annual customer housing billings before deductions; numeric value: 790000.0; detail: Opening total represents billed housing activity, not underlying property value or retained operator revenue. Refundable deposits and taxes collected solely for remittance are outside this modeled total.; label: Landlord rent and utilities; value: Subtract $434,500 for the 55% pass-through share; numeric value: -434500.0; detail: Landlord master-lease rent and utility pass-throughs consume fifty-five percent of billings, leaving $355,500 retained revenue at the canonical forty-five percent retained share.; label: Delivery labor expense; value: Subtract $96,000 for modeled non-owner delivery labor; numeric value: -96000.0; detail: Illustrative contractor and support-labor expense covers placement coordination, field execution, and billing. The owner's full-time seat receives the remaining modeled owner profit rather than a second salary deduction.; label: Property services and systems; value: Subtract $72,000 for services, insurance, and operating systems; numeric value: -72000.0; detail: Illustrative expense covers turnover services, maintenance, commercial insurance, access hardware support, and software subscriptions. Exclude landlord rent and utility amounts already deducted in the pass-through bar.; label: Acquisition and administration; value: Subtract $37,400 for acquisition and administrative expenses; numeric value: -37400.0; detail: Illustrative expense includes referral acquisition, payment processing, bookkeeping, and general administration. Total post-spread operating expense is $205,400 annually, or $17,116.67 monthly before rounding.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $150,100 remains after all modeled operating deductions; numeric value: 150100.0; detail: Closing total is the canonical Base owner profit, not another positive increment. Divide by $790,000 for 19.0% gross-basis margin or by $355,500 for 42.22% retained-basis margin.

text.title: From $790,000 Gross Billings to $150,100 Owner Profit
text.tspan: From $790,000 Gross Billings to $150,100 Owner Profit

circle.title: label: Gross housing billings; value: $790,000 annual customer housing billings before deductions; numeric value: 790000.0; detail: Opening total represents billed housing activity, not underlying property value or retained operator revenue. Refundable deposits and taxes collected solely for remittance are outside this modeled total.

label: Landlord rent and utilities; value: Subtract $434,500 for the 55% pass-through share; numeric value: -434500.0; detail: Landlord master-lease rent and utility pass-throughs consume fifty-five percent of billings, leaving $355,500 retained revenue at the canonical forty-five percent retained share.

label: Delivery labor expense; value: Subtract $96,000 for modeled non-owner delivery labor; numeric value: -96000.0; detail: Illustrative contractor and support-labor expense covers placement coordination, field execution, and billing. The owner's full-time seat receives the remaining modeled owner profit rather than a second salary deduction.

label: Property services and systems; value: Subtract $72,000 for services, insurance, and operating systems; numeric value: -72000.0; detail: Illustrative expense covers turnover services, maintenance, commercial insurance, access hardware support, and software subscriptions. Exclude landlord rent and utility amounts already deducted in the pass-through bar.

label: Acquisition and administration; value: Subtract $37,400 for acquisition and administrative expenses; numeric value: -37400.0; detail: Illustrative expense includes referral acquisition, payment processing, bookkeeping, and general administration. Total post-spread operating expense is $205,400 annually, or $17,116.67 monthly before rounding.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $150,100 remains after all modeled operating deductions; numeric value: 150100.0; detail: Closing total is the canonical Base owner profit, not another positive increment. Divide by $790,000 for 19.0% gross-basis margin or by $355,500 for 42.22% retained-basis margin.

text.title: Assumptions: Formula v2.0 canonical Base totals: $790,000 gross billings, $355,500 retained revenue, and $150,100 annual owner profit. The three operating-expense categories are illustrative allocations totaling $205,400, not supplied line-item forecasts. First and last bars are totals; intervening negative values are deductions. The 45% retained presentation follows the supplied ASC 606 scorecard convention; actual reporting requires the contract-specific principal-versus-agent assessment.
